topic: Signal-aware oracle-adaptation modulus for dependent causal-panel completion on Ferrers masks. Observe one Gaussian rank-r panel Y=M+sigma L_N Z L_T' on a deterministic Ferrers mask with nonvanishing complete slabs, fixed-rank incoherent M, bounded slab Gram geometry, and unknown separable covariance whose inverse-Cholesky factors have bounded spectra and matched row-and-column polynomial tails. For a diffuse missing-cell causal target psi_W(M), define the truth-specific covariance-minimum tangent-balancing score and the minimax L2 distance from all feasible observed-data statistics to its oracle linearization. Derive a primitive target-sensitive necessary-and-sufficient adaptation condition retaining the unavoidable mean-tangent learning cost; construct an observable same-panel residual and tangent-balanced score, feasible variance calibration, and uniform Wald coverage on the adaptation region; and prove matching legal Gaussian lower experiments plus the non-oracle risk frontier outside it. Consumers are Ben-Michael and Feller's right-to-carry reanalysis and Choi-Yuan's SEC Tick Size Pilot analysis. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: An exact rank-one loading-class minimax theorem was derived: for post-period weights h, oracle-reproduction risk is comparable to sigma sqrt((||h||^2+1/m)/m) min(1,sigma/(a sqrt(n))); an observable unknown-signal tangent-balanced statistic attains it with feasible variance calibration. Exact known-separable-covariance profiling gives temporal information J=S_x P_T+S_b P_C and agrees with direct GLS checks below 1.2e-15. Matched-tail and paired-loading counterexamples were checked, while no published collision was verified. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a primitive uniform target-sensitive L2 bound for the joint adaptive-score and rank-curvature remainder when both factor spaces and both nonparametric innovation factors are estimated from the same Ferrers panel, with a matching legal posterior-risk lower experiment. EARLY KILL TEST: On the half-by-half L mask with unknown rank-one row/time directions and unknown nonstationary exact-one-banded innovations, derive the same-panel residual-score remainder and matching posterior lower experiment for both one-period and full-rectangle averages; pivot if this requires supplied factor directions, an independent panel, or stronger covariance regularity. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/panel_ferrers_cholesky_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: What primitive target-sensitive condition is necessary and sufficient for an observable Ferrers-panel estimator to reproduce the known-covariance oracle linearization, including the unavoidable cost of learning the mean tangent, and what is the matching non-oracle risk frontier when that condition fails?

source_refs.claim: For general matrix linear forms, asymptotic variance depends on alignment with the singular spaces rather than merely on sparsity of the functional.
source_refs.author: Dong Xia and Ming Yuan
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.claim: They give rate-optimal recovery of an average treatment effect under general intervention patterns using a treatment-pattern/tangent-space condition, but not an unknown-covariance oracle-adaptation theorem.
source_refs.author: Vivek F. Farias, Andrew A. Li, and Tianyi Peng

source_refs.claim: They attain semiparametric efficiency for linear low-rank models under spiked signals, without characterizing truth-specific adaptation to known separable covariance on deterministic Ferrers masks.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Christian Hansen, Yuan Liao, and Yinchu Zhu

source_refs.claim: They prove matching minimax risks for structured matrix recovery under arbitrary entrywise dependence, but address global recovery rather than target-specific causal inference or oracle-linearization distance.
source_refs.author: Jinhang Chai and Jianqing Fan

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest results isolate different pieces: Xia–Yuan expose functional/singular-space alignment; Farias–Li–Peng use tangent orthogonality for a causal average; Chernozhukov et al. establish an efficiency benchmark under spiked low rank; and Chai–Fan construct minimax lower bounds under dependent noise. None minimizes L2 distance over all feasible observed-data statistics to a truth-specific covariance oracle, and none separates covariance learning from the irreducible cost of learning the low-rank tangent. A matching lower experiment must perturb the mean within rank curvature while simultaneously varying legal separable covariance factors without revealing the oracle score. Exact searches for oracle adaptation in low-rank completion, target-sensitive Ferrers functionals, and truth-specific covariance oracles found no direct collision.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A two-sided theorem equating the feasible-to-oracle L2 modulus, up to constants, to an explicit primitive involving the target matrix, Ferrers observation operator, covariance-weighted tangent projection, signal level, and covariance-tail complexity, plus a matching legal Gaussian posterior-risk lower experiment and an explicit risk formula outside the adaptation region.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its functional-first framing and emphasis on singular-space alignment, replacing random-sampling inference by a causal Ferrers-mask oracle-adaptation question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Causal targets are linear forms of an unobserved low-rank panel -> inferential difficulty depends on target alignment with latent spaces -> dependence makes the efficient direction covariance-specific -> characterize exactly when that unavailable oracle direction can be learned.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the norm of the treatment pattern after projection off the low-rank tangent as the near-necessary geometry and debias along that residual direction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested primitive condition is its target-weighted, covariance-metric refinement on a Ferrers observation operator.

method_exemplars.technique: Nuclear-norm initialization followed by rotated factor regressions yields an asymptotically unbiased expansion and semiparametric efficiency.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the oracle efficiency calculation and factor-rotation control against which feasible adaptation must be measured.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct matching minimax lower bounds under dependent matrix noise using deterministic incoherence geometry and legal dependent-noise distributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its lower-bound architecture can be localized to target-directed Gaussian perturbations and augmented with separable-covariance nuisance alternatives.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one construct a same-Ferrers-panel residual and covariance-weighted tangent-balanced estimator for a diffuse missing-cell causal functional, with a target-sensitive joint score-and-curvature remainder, feasible variance calibration, and a matching lower experiment when both covariance factors and both low-rank factor spaces are unknown?

source_refs.excerpt: introduced to make the Stieltjes bias product-rate

source_refs.claim: Their weak-signal MNAR matrix-completion CLT assumes i.i.d. entry noise and leaves dependent noise to future work because its leave-one-out proof relies on independence.
source_refs.author: Jungjun Choi and Ming Yuan
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: They obtain low-rank-completion inference without sample splitting through auxiliary leave-one/cluster-out arguments and allow dependent observation patterns, but not correlated matrix-normal innovations.
source_refs.author: Jungjun Choi, Hyukjun Kwon, and Yuan Liao

source_refs.claim: BAMITA jointly models a low-rank mean, missing entries, and separable residual covariance, but supplies Bayesian multiple imputation rather than a frequentist causal-panel CLT or minimax adaptation result.
source_refs.author: Ziren Jiang, Gen Li, and Eric F. Lock

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior review's Stieltjes product-rate device supplies a one-sided nuisance-error template but no primitive learner analysis; transferring it requires a target-weighted operator or tail-product inequality that simultaneously controls row and column whitening errors, factor-space error, and rank curvature. The direct Choi–Yuan proof boundary is entrywise independence: holding out an entry decouples its score from the auxiliary iterate, whereas separable row-and-time dependence preserves correlation with training residuals. BAMITA shows that the joint mean/covariance model is viable but does not control same-matrix reuse or frequentist coverage. Thus the first load-bearing step is replacing scalar Stieltjes and leave-one-out decoupling by covariance-aware Gaussian conditioning or an innovation filtration while retaining the mean-tangent learning cost. Searches for same-panel residual scores under separable covariance and Ferrers completion found no theorem occupying this pair.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform L2 expansion of an observable same-panel score into its oracle Gaussian linearization plus explicit target-weighted row-tail, column-tail, factor-space, and rank-curvature remainders, together with consistent variance calibration, uniform Wald coverage, and a matching legal Gaussian posterior-risk lower experiment.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from structured causal missingness to weak-signal completion and feasible inference, while making dependent innovations the precise missing rung.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Staggered treatment induces deterministic MNAR blocks -> subgrouped low-rank completion permits weak-signal estimation -> dependent panel residuals invalidate the existing leave-one-out CLT -> obtain same-panel covariance-aware inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Auxiliary leave-one-out and leave-cluster-out estimators prove negligibility of same-sample factor-estimation remainders and yield a feasible CLT.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired theorem has the same data-reuse problem, but its auxiliary construction must be replaced by a correlated-Gaussian innovation version.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate row and column covariance or precision factors from a single matrix-normal realization using modewise sample correlations and sparse graphical regularization, with operator-norm rates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the nearest single-matrix covariance-nuisance machinery needed before propagating covariance-factor error through the causal score.

method_exemplars.technique: Project the treatment-pattern matrix off the low-rank tangent space and debias the nuclear-norm solution using the resulting orthogonal direction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed tangent-balanced score is the covariance-weighted analogue of this treatment-mask orthogonalization.

open_problems.open_problem: Can matched polynomial-tail inverse-Cholesky factors for both panel modes be estimated from low-rank-contaminated residuals on a deterministic Ferrers mask at rates sufficient for covariance-oracle causal inference from a single matrix?

source_refs.claim: GEMINI recovers row and column covariance and precision matrices from one matrix-normal realization under sparsity, showing that structured single-matrix separable covariance learning is possible.
source_refs.author: Shuheng Zhou

source_refs.claim: They obtain rate-optimal estimators and minimax lower bounds for separable bandable row and column covariance, but not from a single incomplete panel with an estimated low-rank mean.
source_refs.author: Yichi Zhang, Weining Shen, and Dehan Kong
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: They estimate penalized row and column precision matrices from one transposable matrix and use observed-data EM for missing values, but restrict the mean and do not provide causal-target coverage.
source_refs.author: Genevera I. Allen and Robert Tibshirani

source_refs.claim: BAMITA estimates a low-rank mean and separable residual covariance with missing tensor entries, but gives no frequentist masked-residual covariance rate or causal-score propagation theorem.
source_refs.author: Ziren Jiang, Gen Li, and Eric F. Lock

open_problems.why_unsolved: The near-collision literature either assumes a zero or additive mean, uses independent replicated matrices, or provides Bayesian computation without uniform frequentist theory. With a low-rank mean estimated from the same Ferrers panel, residual cross-products contain structured tangent-estimation bias; the mask gives different effective replication counts for different Cholesky rows, and the Kronecker factors require scale normalization. The first proof step that changes from GEMINI or bandable covariance estimation is concentration of the modewise residual Gram matrices after projection through an estimated low-rank tangent and under nonrectangular observation. Searches combining low-rank mean, single matrix, separable covariance, and Ferrers masks found modeling neighbors but no matching frequentist theorem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A normalized estimator of both inverse-Cholesky factors with uniform operator, row-sum, and target-quadratic-form error bounds under Ferrers missingness and estimated low-rank residuals, together with a lower bound and a necessary-and-sufficient score-negligibility corollary.

writing_exemplar.why: It most closely motivates why missing-value uncertainty changes when correlated residual structure is learned jointly with a low-rank mean; the destination should be recast as frequentist causal-panel calibration.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Incomplete panels require low-rank imputation -> residual dependence contains information beyond the low-rank signal -> separable covariance is parsimonious enough to learn -> establish when same-panel covariance learning is accurate enough for causal-target inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit opposite-mode coordinates as effective replicates, normalize modewise sample correlations, and regularize the two precision matrices with graphical-lasso bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the canonical proof that both covariance modes can be learned from one matrix; the new work must quantify mask and mean-estimation contamination.

method_exemplars.technique: Use rank-one Kronecker approximation plus banding or tapering and match the estimator with a minimax covariance lower bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Polynomial Cholesky tails are structurally analogous to their bandable covariance class, and their upper/lower-rate template can be transported to inverse-Cholesky nuisance learning.

open_problems.open_problem: How do the efficient tangent-balanced score, oracle-adaptation condition, lower risk, and feasible variance change when the Ferrers-panel causal target is an event-time rectangle average rather than a one-calendar-period cohort average?

source_refs.claim: They note that event-time effects aggregate across calendar times and therefore across different right singular vectors or factors, so the asymptotic-normality argument and variance may differ from Choi–Yuan's calendar-time estimand.
source_refs.author: Eli Ben-Michael and Avi Feller
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association discussion, forthcoming

source_refs.claim: Their variance formula for a general matrix linear form depends on alignment with the left and right singular spaces, implying that one-period and rectangle targets need not share inferential difficulty.
source_refs.author: Dong Xia and Ming Yuan
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B

source_refs.claim: Partially pooled synthetic controls show that error for staggered-adoption averages depends separately on unit-level and pooled imbalance, making target aggregation a first-class design choice.
source_refs.author: Eli Ben-Michael, Avi Feller, and Jesse Rothstein
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Ben-Michael and Feller pose the target change directly. Under separable covariance, an event-time rectangle combines distinct temporal factors and correlated innovation coordinates, so its covariance-minimum representer is not generally an average of calendar-time representers; the tangent-learning remainder can shrink or grow depending on target diffusion across both modes. The first proof step that changes is the oracle GLS projection: the target weight matrix must be projected jointly against all calendar-specific tangent directions before controlling estimated-score error. Searches for event-time matrix completion with separable covariance, event-time Ferrers variance, and calendar/event tangent balancing found no result resolving this interaction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Closed-form covariance-weighted oracle scores and adaptation moduli for both target classes, matching target-specific Gaussian lower experiments, feasible estimators with a joint CLT and consistently estimable cross-calendar covariance, and a theorem characterizing when exactly one of the two targets lies in the oracle-adaptation region.

writing_exemplar.why: Adopt its applied estimand-first distinction between calendar and event time and its right-to-carry example, then make the unresolved variance statement precise.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Calendar-time averages mix treatment durations -> event-time effects are often the substantive target -> low-rank event-time aggregation crosses different right factors -> derive its target-specific efficient score and inference boundary.

method_exemplars.technique: Debias and project a general matrix linear form, with variance determined by alignment with empirical singular spaces.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An event-time rectangle is a structured linear form whose row/time factor alignment must be retained rather than collapsed to support size.

method_exemplars.technique: Separate unit-specific from pooled imbalance and optimize partially pooled weights for staggered-adoption averages.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its two-component balancing geometry provides the destination-side analogue for separating target directions before covariance-weighted tangent balancing.

method_exemplars.technique: Split Ferrers or staggered missingness into estimable submatrices, debias each low-rank completion, and combine group estimates into a feasible CLT.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The calendar-time baseline and its combination step are the exact objects that must be rederived for event-time aggregation and dependent innovations.

open_problems.open_problem: Can honest causal-target inference over Ferrers panels adapt simultaneously to a long tail of weak or over-specified low-rank components and unknown separable dependence?

source_refs.claim: Their right-to-carry analysis emphasizes small panels with high condition numbers and a long tail of small but non-negligible latent factors.
source_refs.author: Eli Ben-Michael and Avi Feller
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association discussion, forthcoming

source_refs.claim: They show that rank over-estimation produces a non-negligible implicit ridge bias and construct a CLT robust to pre-specified rank at least as large as the truth, but not under Ferrers missingness with unknown matrix-normal covariance.
source_refs.author: Jungjun Choi, Hyukjun Kwon, and Yuan Liao
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: They prove possibility and impossibility results for honest rank-adaptive matrix-completion confidence sets, with unknown noise variance creating model-dependent barriers.
source_refs.author: Alexandra Carpentier, Olga Klopp, Matthias Löffler, and Richard Nickl

source_refs.claim: Their semiparametrically efficient low-rank inference uses a spiked model, leaving the transition from strong spikes to long weak tails outside its main efficiency theorem.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Christian Hansen, Yuan Liao, and Yinchu Zhu

open_problems.why_unsolved: Exact fixed rank suppresses the empirical regime highlighted by Ben-Michael–Feller, while rank-robust and honest-adaptation results currently assume simpler observation and noise experiments. Unknown separable covariance makes weak singular directions hard to distinguish from colored noise, and over-estimation changes the causal functional through an implicit ridge bias rather than variance alone. The first proof step that changes is replacement of a fixed tangent projector by a data-dependent enlarged spectral space while tracking ridge bias, target alignment, and covariance-factor error uniformly. Searches for rank-adaptive Ferrers panels, weak factors with separable covariance, and unknown-rank dependent causal completion found no direct theorem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An honest confidence interval for a stated diffuse causal functional over an approximate-low-rank class with weak spectral tails, with an explicit adaptation region in tail energy, target alignment, and covariance complexity and a matching impossibility theorem outside that region.

writing_exemplar.why: Its small-panel, ill-conditioned right-to-carry example supplies the concrete empirical reason exact fixed rank is inadequate.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Policy panels are small and ill-conditioned -> a few strong factors coexist with a long weak tail -> fixed-rank inference hides uncertainty from that tail -> determine when target-specific honest adaptation remains possible under colored noise.

method_exemplars.technique: Use diversified projections with an over-specified rank and explicitly correct the implicit ridge-type bias induced by the enlarged low-rank space.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same bias appears when a weak Ferrers-panel factor is retained or discarded, but it must be combined with masked covariance-aware scoring.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce honest rank adaptation to composite testing, construct adaptive confidence sets where possible, and prove impossibility where noise uncertainty makes ranks indistinguishable.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its testing lower bounds provide the natural template for the requested target-local adaptation boundary with an additional separable-covariance nuisance.

method_exemplars.technique: Characterize and attain the efficient score for low-rank linear functionals after rotation-aligned factor estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This gives the strong-spike benchmark from which the weak-tail target-specific frontier must depart.

literature_map:
1. Athey, Bayati, Doudchenko, Imbens, and Khosravi (JASA 2021; arXiv:1710.10251) establish causal-panel nuclear-norm completion under policy-induced, serially structured missingness, but not covariance-aware inference.
2. Bai and Ng (arXiv:1910.06677) use tall and wide complete slabs to estimate factors and loadings and obtain counterfactual limit theory under strong-factor geometry.
3. Xiong and Pelger (Journal of Econometrics 2023; arXiv:1910.08273) provide factor and imputation inference under general missing patterns; Su and Wang (Journal of Econometrics 2025; DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2025.106022) extend least-squares factor inference to block and staggered patterns.
4. Choi and Yuan (JASA 2024; arXiv:2308.02364) are the nearest causal-panel anchor: deterministic block or staggered MNAR, weak signals, debiasing, and feasible CLTs, but their noise is i.i.d. and they leave dependent innovations open because leave-one-out becomes difficult.
5. Choi, Kwon, and Liao (Journal of Econometrics 2024; arXiv:2307.16370) solve same-sample low-rank-completion inference through auxiliary leave-one/cluster-out arguments, while allowing dependence in observation patterns rather than residual innovations.
6. Xia and Yuan (JRSSB 2021; arXiv:1909.00116) show that inference for matrix linear forms is target-alignment-sensitive; their random-sampling, independent-noise experiment does not cover Ferrers masks or learned covariance.
7. Farias, Li, and Peng (NeurIPS 2021; arXiv:2106.02780) make treatment-mask/tangent orthogonality central and prove rate-optimal ATE recovery for general intervention patterns; their CLT remains an independent-noise result.
8. Chernozhukov, Hansen, Liao, and Zhu (Annals of Statistics 2023; arXiv:2107.02602) give semiparametrically efficient low-rank inference under spiked signals, furnishing an oracle benchmark but not an unknown-separable-covariance adaptation frontier.
9. Ben-Michael and Feller (2026 discussion; arXiv:2602.21314) directly flag event-time aggregation, heteroskedastic or staggered inference, structured tuning, diagnostics, small panels, and long weak-factor tails; their right-to-carry reanalysis supplies the main consumer-facing motivation.
10. Zhou's GEMINI (Annals of Statistics 2014; arXiv:1209.5075) proves that both covariance modes can be estimated from a single matrix-normal realization under sparsity; Zhang, Shen, and Kong (JASA 2023; arXiv:2004.05281) give minimax-rate bandable separable covariance estimation.
11. Allen and Tibshirani (AOAS 2010; arXiv:0906.3465) handle one transposable matrix and missing-data EM with penalized row and column precision, but only a restricted mean and no causal-target inference.
12. Jiang, Li, and Lock's BAMITA (Biostatistics 2025; arXiv:2410.23412) is the closest modeling collision—joint low-rank mean, missing entries, and separable residual covariance—but is Bayesian multiple imputation without a frequentist minimax or Ferrers causal theorem.
13. Chai and Fan (Annals of Statistics 2025; arXiv:2401.02520) allow arbitrary entrywise dependence and matching minimax recovery risks, yet do not deliver target-specific inference, covariance adaptation, or deterministic Ferrers completion.
14. Exact searches for Ferrers masks plus separable-covariance causal completion and for target-specific oracle adaptation found no published collision; the needed ingredients remain split across causal MNAR completion, single-matrix covariance estimation, and low-rank functional inference.
